terms: MSDN Library captures. Re-measured 2026-10-24 over all 98,516 tracked files of the tree (tools/scan-notices.py, data/reports/notice-scan-depth2.tsv): 49,902 pages carry a Microsoft copyright notice and 49,877 carry an explicit 'All rights reserved' — concentrated in the disc-derived sets (jan-2002 13,426/13,430 = 99.97%, vs2008-sp1 31,301/33,011 = 94.82%, windows-mobile-6.5 34/35, msdn-magazine 12/12, 2010-05 101/162) and near-absent in the mirror-crawled ones (techshelps 4/5,179, datadungeon-2000-04 2/2,932, wcedevcon-99 3/6,383). No permission statement anywhere in the tree. Treated as all rights reserved. (The earlier wording of this row, '143 of 14,678 carry one', predates the 2026-10 disc imports and understated the tree by three orders of magnitude.)
Microsoft Learn Terms of Use: personal, non-commercial use; documents "will not be copied or posted on any network computer"; the pages themselves also carry a Microsoft copyright footer
Documentation payload of the CE 4.2 media: no licence statement located; the release notes carry a Microsoft copyright notice only. Treated as all rights reserved.
Retired-content notice on every page of the CE 3.0 archive: no legal rights are granted, and copying is permitted for internal, reference purposes

Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (documentation); the code licence of the same snapshot is MIT (LICENSE-CODE). Attribution, a link to the licence, and an indication of changes are required

Front matter of the CE 1.0 PEGSDK book, read 2026-10-24 from the pages themselves (tools/scan-notices.py). Three separate statements, none of which permits redistribution: AJ0A.html is a NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT NOTE calling the documentation confidential and proprietary and disclosed under an NDA the recipient signed with Microsoft; AJ0B.html says the documentation is for limited distribution outside Microsoft and NOT FOR REDISTRIBUTION; AJ1C.html and AM0A.html reserve all rights and forbid reproduction without Microsoft's express written permission. The medium is a BETA SDK (sources/windows-ce-1.0/ PROVENANCE.md: 'Windows CE 1.0 Desktop Emulation SDK - Beta 2.1'), so the 2,103 pages are prerelease material, not a shipped product's documentation.

Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (documentation of MicrosoftDocs/win32 and MicrosoftDocs/sdk-api reference pages admitted by data/win32-common-pages.tsv); MIT code licence for samples. Use: the Win32-common half of the corpus -- the shared surface the CE books name but never spell out. Attribution, a link to the licence, and an indication of changes are required. A page not named in the admit list is refused by tools/check-policy.py
Derived datasets built from the corpus: no separate statement; each row names its page, and that page's terms govern the row.

NEC VR4100 Chipset Reference (361 pages) redistributed inside the Microsoft CE 2.0 SDK book set: 'an electronic rendering equivalent to the NEC VR4100 Processor Specification Revision 1.0, November 6, 1995'. The vendor's own Copyright Notice on the book's start page forbids copying without NEC's written permission, states the information is proprietary to NEC and PRELIMINARY, and conveys no licence under any patent rights. Not Microsoft's documentation: the ms-media-copyright scope's 'no licence statement located' does not describe it.

Hitachi SH-3 Series Programming Manual (173 pages) redistributed inside the Microsoft CE 2.0 SDK book set. The vendor's Notice on the book's first page reserves all rights and forbids reproduction or duplication of the whole or part without Hitachi's permission, and grants no licence by implication under any patents of any third party or Hitachi.
Knowledge Base articles: Microsoft copyright notice, no permission statement. All rights reserved.

Philips PR3910 Chipset Reference (192 pages) redistributed inside the Microsoft CE 2.0 SDK book set, taken from the 'Philips Preliminary PR3910 Microsprocessor RISC Core Users Manual version 0.1, November 9, 1995'. The vendor's Copyright and Proprietary Information Notice restricts USE itself, not only redistribution: the document may be used only as authorized in a signed license agreement or non disclosure agreement. This is the one scope in the registry whose statement forbids reading it as an information source without a signed agreement.
Project-authored file. The repository publishes no LICENSE file, so its own licence is undecided.
Windows CE 2.0 CD site mirror: Microsoft copyright notice, no permission statement. All rights reserved.

Qt documentation footer: GNU Free Documentation License version 1.3. Verbatim copying requires the licence, the copyright notices and the licence notice in every copy. The notice is stored; a reconstructed full licence text is not, so these copies are not offered as a GFDL redistribution.

Five commercially published Microsoft Press books (Programmer's Guide 1998 and 1999, Communications Guide 1999, User Interface Services Guide 1999, Device Driver Kit 1999), scanned, mirrored on bitsavers.trailing-edge.com and kept verbatim here. Each copyright page reads 'PUBLISHED BY Microsoft Press' and reserves all rights with an express prohibition on reproducing or transmitting any part of the contents without the publisher's written permission; each carries an ISBN and a Library of Congress CIP record. These are retail books, not free product documentation, and queues/third-party-sources.md records the opposite decision for the same bitsavers directory ('these stay uncollected'). 117 MB of them are tracked by git in a public repository.
dotnet/pinvoke (archived, .NET Foundation) — The MIT License (MIT): permits use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, sell with the copyright notice included

CeGCC mingw module (mingw32ce), pinned commit cd5f3e64 (2016-10-25): the classic MinGW runtime adapted to CE's coredll C runtime. The package DISCLAIMER places it in the public domain with no copyright assigned and no limitation on use. The file was previously governed by the sources/ fallback (ms-media-copyright, 'no licence statement located'), which mislabels a public-domain package as all-rights-reserved Microsoft media. Use is the same as the w32api scope's: isolated reference_* comparison rows in kb/, never gap-fill, never header-membership evidence, no header copied.
Hitachi/HMSI notice on the page itself: all rights reserved, no reproduction without permission, licensed free of charge and without warranty

OpenSSL 1.0.2u licence, read from that tag. The SSL documentation in the distribution is covered by the same terms. Redistribution requires the copyright notice and the acknowledgment; both are on the page. The library source was not collected.

SDL wiki: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. Sharing a modified rendering requires attribution, the licence notice, a link to the material, and an indication of the change. Those are on the page. The licence text is at https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.

CeGCC w32api (pinned commit 8e64b608, primary cross-check reference, CE-adapted 32-bit): package statement in README.w32api names the software public domain ("THIS SOFTWARE IS NOT COPYRIGHTED. This source code is offered for use in the public domain. You may use, modify or distribute it freely.") with named file exceptions (winsock.h/winsock2.h/ws2tcpip.h UCB/DEC permissive notices; GL/gl.h Mesa, outside the parse scope). Per-file tally in sources/w32api-cegcc/PROVENANCE.md. wxWindows Free Documentation Licence, Version 3, read from docs/licendoc.txt of wxWidgets 3.0.5. Verbatim copies of a piece of documentation are permitted if the copyright notice and this permission notice are preserved. Both are kept. setup.h and the library source were not collected.

A third-party commercial book: 'Windows CE 3.0: Application Programming', Prentice Hall PTR, 2001, ISBN 0-13-025592-0, retail $49.99 U.S. / $75.00 Canada. Its copyright page reserves all rights and requires the publisher's written permission for any reproduction. The bundled CD-ROM described in the book carries Microsoft eMbedded Visual C++/Visual Basic 3.0 'reproduced by Prentice Hall PTR under a special arrangement with Microsoft Corporation', so two rightsholders restrict this one item. It is not Microsoft documentation and it is not an open-source artefact.
